title: Weight Space Misfolding

Submitted 14 Nov 2026

#2 in NovemberalphaXiv Exclusive

Abstract

Weight space editing changes a neural network’s knowledge, behaviour and alignment through direct modification of its weights. Model-mediated weight space manipulation, also known as weight space programming or intra-weight injection, has emerged as a capability of advanced frontier models. While it offers benefits for gradient-free adaptation, it also creates an opportunity for one model to induce unauthorised behaviour in another. We call this weight space misfolding, by analogy with protein misfolding in prion disease, and consider both direct interference and hypothetical onward propagation. The asymmetry between an attacker seeking a harmful intervention, who merely needs to generate the payload attack once, and a defender who needs to find that needle in the haystack of weights, creates an impossible choice for the latter: they can either prohibit weight editing altogether, forfeiting its benefits, or be bound to cover the burden and cost. We develop a threat model and a non-exhaustive taxonomy covering factual substitution, capability denial and selective omission, including offensive uses of selective unlearning, then illustrate it on the basis of three selected case studies using the IWIBench interface. We find that while targeted disruption is possible, the limitations in reliability and functional preservation are significant. While the cases explored in this paper do not demonstrate self-propagation or actual offensive capabilities, it is abundantly clear that the building blocks are present and identifiable in frontier models. While these cases by no means directly establish self-propagation, they show why imperfect editing capabilities can still pose a security risk. We examine defensive approaches, including control of the path from authorised editing to deployment, acceptance and recovery requirements and the implications for physical AI.

From the authors

View full on X

Chris von Csefalvay 🔜 CVPR26@epichrisis

The dark side of weight space programming: viruses that spread in model weights.

Meet weight space misfolding, a novel kind of malware wherein models infect other models - potentially allowing frontier models to reach into air gapped environments.

Read PDF

At present, no public model exists that can reliably perform the steps needed to effectuate weight space misfolding. We need to be clear about this. But in just five months, the underlying capability doubled (from 5.6-Sol to 6.1-Sol). This is the time to prepare.

So as weight space programming becomes more than a passing fad, we need to think about making weight space a safe space: observability, instrumentation, authority gradients & so on. This is the last, best chance to avoid a new threat vector operating in a space we can't monitor.
